name: layout
description: Foundations contract for the layout & spacing system: containers, section layouts, section rhythm, and content grids. UIDS owns the vocabulary (spacing scale, gutters, breakpoints, container caps); uids_base (SiteNow) is the downstream consumer whose Layout Builder classes express these patterns. Not a component — no Vue code, no Figma component set.

figma.note: Documentation page (container frames + layout grids), not a component set. space/* and layout/* variables live in the Primitives and Semantic collections.

options.name: container
options.description: Section container behavior: outer width and page margin. Standard: 1.25rem side margins, caps/centers at 81.875em from the page-container breakpoint. Narrow: caps at 63.75em from md. Wide: caps at 100em with 1.875rem side padding at page-container. Full: viewport-wide with 1.25rem/3rem margins. Edge: no outer margins.

code.notes: standard's visual behavior is largely the default container mixin; the modifier class adds little

options.name: layout
options.description: Section column structure. Mobile-first: every multi-column layout stacks below md (980px), then adopts its ratio. Ratios are authored patterns, not a universal 12-column grid.

code.notes: class families live in uids_base scss/layouts/; 50/50 and 33/34/33 consume the shared UIDS grid mixins

options.name: contentGrid
options.description: Modular grid for repeated content (cards, lists, feeds) inside a region. Activation is gated by parent region width (inner-grid mixin: twocol needs parent >= 50%, threecol/fourcol >= 75%).

options.name: sectionPaddingRemovedTop
options.description: Layout Builder: Remove top spacing (top padding 0)

options.name: sectionPaddingRemovedBottom
options.description: Layout Builder: Remove bottom spacing (bottom padding 0)

options.name: sectionPaddingTopExtra
options.description: Layout Builder: Add extra top spacing (top padding = layout/section/padding/extra)

options.name: sectionPaddingBottomExtra
options.description: Layout Builder: Add extra bottom spacing (bottom padding = layout/section/padding/extra)

options.name: sectionPaddingTopRestored
options.description: Layout Builder: Restore default spacing — TOP EDGE ONLY (see knownIssues)

options.name: columnSpacingRemoved
options.description: Layout Builder: Remove default column spacing (region gaps and stacked-region spacing)

options.name: columnSpacingIncreased
options.description: Layout Builder: Increase default column spacing — region gaps step to 7.8125rem / 125px (space/781). Accepted 2026-08-24; like every other column-spacing / section-padding option the class ships from uids_base, and it is not yet authored there. See changes[].

options.name: sectionOrderReversed
options.description: Layout Builder: Reverse column order on mobile

options.name: blockPadding
options.description: Local padding on a block, from src/scss/abstracts/_utility-classes.scss:34-73. Unlike every other option on this contract these classes ship FROM UIDS, not from uids_base. Base is 3rem (space/300), --minimal is 2rem (space/200), --extra is 6rem (space/600). The .block-padding and .element--padding namespaces are declared as one selector list and are exactly equivalent — neither is preferred.

code.notes: right/bottom/left follow top's pattern in both namespaces. all-sm is the exception: .element--padding__all--sm is declared on its own (line 71), has NO .block-padding twin, and resolves to 1.25rem (space/125) rather than the 3rem the rest of the __all family uses.

figma.notes: Contract-only, and this whole contract is a documentation page rather than a component set — there is no variant axis to map to. A local padding utility is applied per placement by a Drupal author; the Figma equivalent is setting padding on the frame you are drawing, not picking a variant. Foundations / Layout documents the SCALE these classes draw from (the space/* frame, 120:3), which is the part a designer needs.

options.name: blockMargin
options.description: Local margin on a block, from _utility-classes.scss:104-139. Base is 1.05rem (space/105 = layout/block/stack/compact); --extra holds that value below sm and steps to 2rem (layout/block/stack/extra) from sm. In stacked Layout Builder regions these are OVERRIDES on the 1.6rem default sibling rhythm, not additions to it — see behavior.

code.notes: left/right are the odd ones: they apply ONLY from sm (no mobile value at all), where top/bottom apply at every width. See knownIssues.

figma.notes: Contract-only — see blockPadding's note. Additionally, the part of this option a designer would most want drawn (that in a stacked region these are OVERRIDES on the 1.6rem default sibling rhythm, not additions) is a uids_base region behavior with no Figma surface at all: layout/block/stack/default is a variable, but nothing in the file arranges sibling blocks to show it being overridden.

options.name: logicalPadding
options.description: CSS logical-property padding utilities, _utility-classes.scss:75-102. A separate, much smaller scale from the block utilities above: --sm is 0.5rem (space/50) and --md is 1rem (space/100). These ship from UIDS.

code.notes: There is deliberately no `inline-sm` entry — .padding--inline--sm is not declared. See knownIssues.

figma.notes: Contract-only — see blockPadding's note. Logical properties have no Figma expression in any case: the file has no writing-mode dimension, so padding-inline-start and padding-left are the same edge on the canvas and the distinction these classes exist to make cannot be drawn.

geometryNotTokenized.sidebar-ratio: 24.25% sidebar / 72.75% content, separated by 3% right margin on the sidebar (md+); content 100% when sidebar hidden
geometryNotTokenized.grid-minmax: content-grid tracks: twocol minmax(46.7%, 1fr), threecol minmax(29.74%, 1fr), fourcol minmax(21%, 1fr) — auto-fill
geometryNotTokenized.inner-grid-breakpoint: 58.125em (930px) internal breakpoint in _grid-mixins.scss for three/four-col inner grids and twocol's fixed 1fr 1fr switch — NOT one of the tokenized breakpoints
geometryNotTokenized.onecol-fixed-padding: 1.1rem top/bottom (space/110), a condensed band outside the section rhythm
geometryNotTokenized.twocol-25-75-gaps: 1.5rem gap at sm -> 3rem at page-container (only content grid whose gap steps at page-container)
geometryNotTokenized.block-margin-utilities: 1.05rem base (space/105), --extra variants step to 2rem at sm; __right/__left have no mobile value
geometryNotTokenized.strays: 0.2rem and 1.75rem appear once each in uids_base layouts; left raw deliberately

behavior: Mobile-first: all multi-column layouts stack below md (980px); stacked regions use layout/gutter/height/mobile (2rem) bottom spacing
Section rhythm steps at sm (768px), NOT md: padding goes 1.25rem -> 3rem top/bottom; the first section removes top padding
Adjacent sections with the same background treatment (none/gold/black/gray/brain variants) merge: the second removes its top padding

Block stacking: sibling blocks in Layout Builder regions get 1.6rem top spacing (layout/block/stack/default); .block-margin__top reduces to 1.05rem, __top--extra becomes 2rem from sm, __default--removed zeroes it — the margin utilities are authored overrides on the default rhythm, not purely additive
Containers cap/center at the page-container breakpoint (1350px): standard 81.875em, wide 100em + 1.875rem side padding; narrow caps earlier (md, 63.75em)
Content grids: non-grid lists stack at 2rem; grid gaps are 2rem mobile -> 3rem from sm (desktop gutter)

OWNERSHIP SPLIT, and it is the thing to get right about this contract: the container / layout / contentGrid / section-padding / column-spacing / section-order options are uids_base classes — UIDS owns their vocabulary and tokens but ships no CSS for them, so they can only be documented here and reproduced in claude-design/layout.css for previews. The blockPadding / blockMargin / logicalPadding options are the opposite: they ship from THIS repo, via src/scss/abstracts/_utility-classes.scss forwarded through uids-core.scss:6

The .block-* and .element--* namespaces are the same rule set. _utility-classes.scss declares `.block-padding, .element--padding` (line 34) and `.block-margin, .element--margin` (line 104) as selector lists, so every modifier exists under both names with identical behavior and neither is canonical

Breakpoint reference. Below sm (768): sections pad 1.25rem, full-width containers keep a 1.25rem outer margin, multi-region layouts stack with 2rem between regions, content grids gap 2rem. From sm: section padding becomes 3rem and the block-margin --extra step goes 1.05rem -> 2rem. From md (980): column ratios engage, full-width containers take 3rem outer margins, desktop grid gaps are 3rem, and the mobile stacked-region spacing is dropped. From page-container (1350): standard containers centre at 81.875em, wide expands to 100em with 1.875rem side padding, and grid--twocol--25-75 steps its gap 1.5rem -> 3rem

changes.summary: Accepted the Layout Builder option 'Increase default column spacing' (column-spacing__increased, 7.8125rem / 125px) and minted space/781 for it.
changes.reasoning: The option had sat marked PROPOSED at 567:78 in the layout exploration doc with nothing behind it — no primitive, no class, no contract entry — which is exactly the ambiguous state that makes a later reader unable to tell a deliberate omission from an oversight. The design system owner ruled it accepted on 2026-08-24, so it is recorded as public shape here first, contract-first, ahead of the CSS. Two consequences worth stating plainly. First, space/781 breaks nothing but does bend the scale's naming rule: 7.8125rem is 781.25, and the step name rounds to 781 the same way space/32, space/62 and space/187 round from 32.5, 62.5 and 187.5 — the name is a label, the value is authoritative. Second, this is the ownership split doing its job in the awkward direction: UIDS owns the vocabulary and the token, uids_base ships the class, and the class does not exist downstream yet. Until it lands in /Users/bspeare/acquia/uiowa, check-token-consumers will report --uiowa-space-781 as ORPHAN. That warning is deliberately NOT silenced via tokens/orphans-allowed.json, because it is a true statement and a live to-do rather than a downstream contract already honoured.

changes.summary: Declined to mint the six proposed semantic layout tokens (layout/block/padding/{default,minimal,extra,sm}, layout/logical/padding/{sm,md}).
changes.reasoning: The design system owner's ruling, 2026-08-24. The utilities were already bound directly to the primitives (space/200, /300, /600, /125, /50, /100) and every checker is green, so the semantic tier would buy naming and cost six more custom properties on a token surface already carrying 39 orphan and doc-only warnings, plus six more Figma variables that each need codeSyntax.WEB set to stay visible to check-figma. Recorded so a later reader does not re-propose it as an obvious gap: the indirection was considered and judged not to earn its keep.

changes.summary: The block/element padding and margin utilities, and the logical-padding utilities, were admitted to this contract as the blockPadding / blockMargin / logicalPadding options.
changes.reasoning: They were the only UIDS-SHIPPED CSS in the layout system with no contract entry at all — roughly 25 classes forwarded from uids-core.scss that no view described. That gap is what let their values sit as raw literals (3rem, 2rem, 6rem, 0.5rem, 1rem) while the token layer that was supposed to govern them had zero consumers in src/scss. Admitting them is ordinary contract-first work on a contract already in the set, not a migration: the CLOSED ruling governs bringing NEW components in, and this contract's kind is foundation. Rendering is unchanged — no class was added, removed or restyled.

changes.summary: Declined to rename the utility --sm / --md suffixes despite the two-scale collision now recorded in knownIssues.
changes.reasoning: Faithful names lose an argument about clarity and win the one about findability: someone reading .padding--block--sm in a Drupal template needs the grep to land, and a corrected name would break that for every existing consumer to fix a confusion the contract can simply state. Same call, same reasoning, as leaving the $md spacing-vs-breakpoint collision in place. Recorded so a later reader does not mistake the collision for an oversight.

changes.summary: Recorded that .element--padding__all--sm is intended to supersede .padding--block--sm, and that the two are NOT interchangeable.
changes.reasoning: The design system owner's intent, 2026-08-24. The trap is that the replacement reads like a rename and is not one: .element--padding__all--sm sets `padding` on all four sides at 1.25rem, while .padding--block--sm sets `padding-block` only, at 0.5rem. Swapping one for the other adds inline padding that was never there and multiplies the block padding by 2.5. Both still ship and live sites depend on the legacy one, so neither is removed here — tokenize as-shipped.

knownIssues: layout/section/padding/{mobile,default} are a PARALLEL VOCABULARY that nothing reads. Production authors .layout__container's padding from the gutter variables instead — uids_base scss/global.scss:153-161 uses $mobile-width-gutter and $desktop-width-gutter, which resolve to layout/gutter/width/{mobile,desktop}. The section-padding tokens hold the same two values ({space.125}, {space.300}) under a different name, and their only consumer anywhere is claude-design/layout.css

Consequence of the parallel vocabulary above, and the reason it is recorded rather than fixed: editing layout/section/padding/default to change section rhythm moves the Claude Design preview and NOTHING in production. Verified 2026-08-24 by grepping the authored uids_base SCSS — zero reads of var(--uiowa-layout-section-padding-*), and only four reads of any --uiowa-* custom property in the entire theme, because uids_base consumes UIDS through Sass variables rather than custom properties. Consolidating the two vocabularies is a 5.x decision

layout/gutter/height/desktop has no consumer at all. Its 4.x source variable $desktop-height-gutter is declared at src/scss/abstracts/_variables.scss:82 and used nowhere in this repo, so the variable was deliberately left holding a literal rather than rebound — pointing it at the token would have made the token look consumed while compiling to nothing

The utility scale uses `sm` for two different values, in two different families: .element--padding__all--sm is 1.25rem (space/125) while .padding--block--sm and the --inline-*--sm pair are 0.5rem (space/50). Same suffix, 2.5x apart. This is the spacing-side twin of the `md` collision recorded below, and it is as-shipped — the names were kept rather than corrected so a grep for the class lands on the token (ruling, 2026-08-24, see changes[])

.padding--inline--sm does not exist. The logical-padding family is otherwise symmetric — block and inline-start and inline-end each have --sm and --md — but the shorthand .padding--inline-- only ships in --md (_utility-classes.scss:100). Authoring one by analogy silently does nothing

.block-margin__left and __right apply only from sm (_utility-classes.scss:117-121, 134-138); they have no mobile value, where __top and __bottom apply at every width. A layout relying on left/right margin below sm gets nothing
section-padding__top-restored restores the TOP edge only; there is no bottom-restore class

section-padding__top-restored does not restore the DEFAULT below sm — it sets a flat 3rem at every width. Production emits `.section-padding__top-restored{padding-top:3rem}` with no media query (verified 2026-08-24 in uids_base assets/css/global.css), while the default section padding below sm is 1.25rem. So an author picking 'Restore default spacing' on a phone gets 2.4x the spacing the label promises, and the two edges of that section stop matching (3rem top, 1.25rem bottom). Distinct from the top-edge-only issue above, and as-shipped: found while building the Foundation/Layout Storybook page, whose diagram reproduces it faithfully rather than quietly rendering the responsive value
The word 'md' means two different things in 4.x SCSS: $md = 1.05rem (a spacing value) vs $break-md / --space-md-width-gutter (breakpoint / 2rem). The space.* scale supersedes the spacing sense.
grid--twocol--50-50 column-gap uses var(--space-lg-width-gutter) while threecol/fourcol use $desktop-width-gutter — same 3rem value via two mechanisms (compile-time vs runtime)
